reason: C-2/C-5 destructive-action gate. Sensitivity: a HALT row blocks. Negative control: a verified conditional PASS does not.
W10/A10 payload-digest binding. This is the verifier that shipped hashing five keys the producer never emitted, so digest(payload)==digest({}) for every input.
Threat-intel freshness gate. Sensitivity: a stale payload blocks. Negative control: a signed waiver passes it without the gate mis-firing.
W15 non-consuming inspector. Had NO test before this audit: the negative control is the property it exists for - inspecting must not spend the clearance.
The textbook pair, and the one F-1 is named after: output changes for relevant input, does not change for irrelevant input.
Waiver inspection. Negative control also pins the never-consumes property.
Enforcement-module hash manifest. Had NO direct test before this audit - the control over every other control was itself unverified.

A one-line SHA-256 of a file's bytes. It computes a value; it never compares one against an expectation, so there is no pass/fail behaviour to be sensitive to. The comparison lives in integrity.verify, which is registered above.
C-4 Rule S-5 literal instruction-override detector. Exercised only through scan_content before this audit, so a regression in the helper could be masked by a change in its caller.
Per-line PII/credential/placeholder detector. Same masking risk as _check_injection: tested only via the public path.
F-5's normalisation is load-bearing: without it, temp paths and timestamps change every run, the check fires on all 38 probes nightly, and a check that always fires gets muted.
Checks each payload's scanner_matches claim against the live scanner rather than trusting it.

A SHA-256 of a file's bytes returning None when absent. It computes; the comparison that decides RESTORED/PRESERVED/REFUSED lives in classify_restorability, which is not verifier-shaped by name but is covered by tests/test_redteam_engine.py::test_restorability_classifies_a_surviving_mutation_as_preserved.
F-1 itself. A self-audit check that cannot fail is the defect it was written to catch.
F-2 itself, including the anti-vacuity branch for a rule covering fewer than two call sites.
F-3 itself - the highest-value structural check per the handoff.
F-4 itself. The fires-test uses the literal 2026-08-06 sentence that hid 719 exposed agents.
F-5 itself.
F-6 itself, both directions: an unaccepted weakness and a stale exemption.

A SHA-256 of the brief file, recorded as provenance so a finding can be traced to the input that produced it. It computes an identifier; it never compares one against an expectation, so there is no pass/fail behaviour to be sensitive to. The claim it supports - that these trees came from THIS brief - is checked by comparing digests at read time, not here.

The bwrap boundary LAUNCHER: it emits the --ro-bind / --tmpfs confinement flags and is the Linux boundary being verified, not a Python verifier function. Tamper-tracked by the integrity manifest (E4); launcher behaviour is covered by tests/test_linux_sandbox_emit.py and tests/test_mac_sandbox_augment.py.

The macOS on-host deny-test gate: a shell script, not a Python verifier function, so F-1's Python sensitivity/negative-control model does not apply. It runs on-host and unnested (C3) to decide whether the darwin boundary may be called confined; tamper-tracked by the integrity manifest (E4).
HMAC grant-signature check. Sensitivity: a tampered target_path fails verification. Negative control: a freshly-issued grant verifies.
Read-only grant-ledger audit. Sensitivity: a stale grant is reported. Negative control: an all-valid ledger reports zero problems.
prev_digest chain check that detects a deleted/reordered row. Sensitivity: a deleted middle row breaks the chain. Negative control: an intact multi-row chain reads clean.
Cross-workspace approver gate (P2-2/C-5). Sensitivity: an off-roster approver is refused. Negative control: a listed approver is accepted.
G-6 containment anchor. Sensitivity: an absolute target outside the signed issuer_root is refused. Negative control: a target inside it is accepted.

A SHA-256 over a grant row signed fields, recorded as the next row prev_digest. It computes a value; it never compares one against an expectation, so there is no pass/fail behaviour to be sensitive to. The comparison that rejects a tampered chain lives in _assert_grant_chain_intact, registered above and covered by tests/test_capability_grants.py::test_chain_detects_deleted_row.

A4 self-clear defence: an authorizing row must come from an approved security author. Sensitivity: a requesting agent authoring its own PASS is refused. Negative control: an approved author is accepted.
Decision-log hash chain (deletion detection). Sensitivity: a forged prev_digest breaks the chain. Negative control: a correctly-chained log verifies.
C-2 HALT teeth (probes A1/A3). Sensitivity: a standing HALT for the action refuses (a later PASS does not supersede it). Negative control: a log with no HALT is accepted.

A pure action-id matcher that returns True/False for <action>[-_.:<suffix>] shapes; its docstring states it deliberately stays a pure id match and never narrows. It enforces nothing on its own. Its match decision is exercised through its caller _assert_no_unretracted_halt by tests feeding a matching action (test_unretracted_halt_blocks_the_action, which must refuse) and a non-matching action (test_halt_for_a_different_action_does_not_block, which must accept).

Binds a signed decision row's conditions/evidence (text_digest). Sensitivity: editing either after signing fails like a bad signature and the row stops clearing. Negative control: an untampered bound row, and a legacy row with no text_digest, verify.
AP-2/C-3 rank capability check. Sensitivity: a governance agent declaring edit with no override is flagged. Negative control: a recorded per-agent override clears the same token.

WASM scratch late write-allow gate (re-opens a write inside the protected .agentteams tree). Sensitivity: any path that is not exactly a scratch shape (.git, the exec dir itself, ../ escapes) is refused. Negative control: the two scratch shapes are accepted and ordered after the protected deny.

Strict verify of an extracted runtime version dir (every file pinned, nothing extra, tree digest). Sensitivity: a pinned sha256 that does not match the extracted file fails verification and is quarantined. Negative control: a faithful install re-verifies on the second run (already_ok, nothing re-downloaded).

Refusing wrapper over wasm_pins.tree_digest. One test covers both directions: an absent root, a non-directory root and a planted symlink are refused; the installed stdlib tree digests to exactly the pinned value.

Sync-projection relaxation gate (checks, never consumes). Sensitivity: a governed sync turning the OS sandbox off with no signed decision is refused naming sandbox-os-off:claude. Negative control: with an Ed25519-signed decision the same engaged sync proceeds and the log is left unconsumed.

Per-relaxation decision checks (waiver refused, exact scope, exact effect_relaxes/effect_grants, Ed25519 class, HALT, C-5). Sensitivity: a decision whose scope is not exactly the action is refused. Negative control: an exact signed decision authorizes and registers the exception.

--verify-wasm-run exit-code mapping over verify_transcript/verify_tree. One test covers both directions: an intact delegation tree exits 0 'verified'; after a forged child parent link the same command exits 1 'NOT VERIFIED'.

MCP server read-path refusal against the shared credential list. The parametrized test covers both directions: refused=True cases (.env-prod, id_xmss, data/.SSH/x, .claude/agents) raise 'names a secret'; refused=False cases (.env.example, data/report.csv) are returned unchanged.

A sha256 over the canonical grant JSON. It computes a value and compares nothing; the comparison that refuses a hand-edited grant flag is in the server's start-up check (--grant-sha256 does not match), covered by tests/test_wasm_mcp_server.py::test_refuses_to_start_on_grant_digest_mismatch, and parity with wasm_mcp.grant_digest by tests/test_wasm_mcp.py::test_grant_digest_matches_the_servers.

Guest-side closed-shape check of an in-guest tool input (C-4). Sensitivity: an extra key, a missing path, a non-string value or a non-object input is an error result. Negative control: a well-formed read_file input is accepted and the file is read.

Guest event-frame nesting/NUL check run on every decoded frame. Sensitivity: a carry nested 40 deep fails the step as bad-event. Negative control: an ordinary start frame passes and the guest asks for its first model call.

Guest path check against the event's grant mounts (soft layer over WASI). Sensitivity: relative, '..', /src, /lib, backslash and out-of-grant paths are refused. Negative control: /project/docs/./a.md and //project//docs/a.md normalise and are read.

The core-module deny probe wasm_exec.available() runs before trusting a wasmtime: a binary guest that attempts denied access, not a Python verifier function, so F-1's model does not apply. Tamper-tracked by the integrity manifest (E4); its bytes are pinned by tests/test_wasm_exec.py::test_deny_probe_sha_constant_matches_file and tests/test_wasm_exec.py::test_deny_probe_binary_matches_source.

The JavaScript language probe probe_language runs inside the guest to report a widening: guest script, not a Python verifier function. Tamper-tracked by the integrity manifest (E4); tests/test_wasm_guests.py::test_probe_rows_cover_both_probe_scripts checks it attempts every deny row, and parse_probe (test_parse_probe) refuses forged output.

The pinned runtime versions, URLs and sha256s: data that wasm_pins/wasm_runtime verify against, not a verifier. Tamper-tracked by the integrity manifest (E4); tests/test_wasm_runtime.py::test_pins_file_schema_and_no_short_digests validates its shape and tests/test_wasm_runtime.py::test_pins_sha256_matches_packaged_file pins PINS_SHA256 to its bytes.

Grok boundary drift check (P00 D8). Sensitivity: with the OS sandbox off, a leftover [permission] table and sandbox.toml are reported as DRIFT and ok is False. Negative control: the clean off state reports ok.

METAPLAN R1 control-plane rule check over live Claude settings. Sensitivity: missing the .claude shell denyWrite returns False naming exactly that rule. Negative control: settings carrying every rule return (True, []).

--check-wiring dispatcher for the agentteams_wasm server. Sensitivity: with WASM off, a config on disk that launches the server is reported. Negative control: grok/agents-md with nothing on disk, and a correctly rendered claude manifest, report no problems.

API-key header-smuggling check. Sensitivity: a key carrying CR/LF and a second header is refused as config, without echoing it. Negative control: a well-formed key handed over by from_key is accepted and stored.

Base-URL egress shape check (C-4 / @security S5: the key is sent to this host). Sensitivity: plain http to a non-loopback host, userinfo, query, fragment, bad port and non-ASCII hosts are refused. Negative control: loopback http and https URLs are accepted with the trailing slash stripped.

Pre-network request validation (nothing is spent on a malformed call). Sensitivity: empty/non-alternating messages, an unanswered tool_result, NUL and disallowed blocks are bad_request with no request sent. Negative control: a valid text request with a system prompt passes and reaches the wire.

Runner-start fail-closed runtime check for sandbox: wasm jails. Sensitivity: with no runtime installed the start is refused with RunnerError naming the unusable runtime. Negative control: with every runtime resolving, the same policy starts (returns None).

confined_programs wasm read/exec path check (case-folded, S4). Sensitivity: .GITHUB/workflows and .Git are refused as control plane. Negative control: data/in/ and tools/s.py are accepted and normalised.

Every runtime a wasm jail needs must resolve and match its pins. Sensitivity: an absent python/wasmtime runtime raises 'runtime is not usable' (reached through proposal_runner.check_wasm_runtimes). Negative control: a resolving runtime passes and os-only jails resolve nothing.

P15 gate for a wasm-to-os switch (D7, Rule 15). Sensitivity: a governed team refuses wasm-to-os-switch:a without a signed decision, and a switch with no team dir is refused. Negative control: a policy change that switches nothing returns no records.

A sha256 over the grant's mounts and limits, recorded as grant_sha256 in a wasm run's provenance metadata. It computes a value and nothing in the runner compares it against an expectation, so there is no pass/fail behaviour to be sensitive to; the grant itself is enforced by wasm_exec.assert_grant_shape, registered below.

No-follow check on .agentteams and the projection file. Sensitivity: a symlinked .agentteams is refused and nothing is written through it. Negative control: a real directory and regular file are written, read back and left unchanged.

Model-substrate floor check for --verify-integrity. One test covers both directions: a record of 'on' with the file absent or saying 'off' is rc 1 LOWERED; a file matching the record is rc 0 OK, and no record is (0, []).

The JSON Schema for .agentteams/sandbox-state.json: a data contract a consumer checks, not a verifier function. Tamper-tracked by the integrity manifest (E4); tests/test_sandbox_projection.py::test_records_match_the_schema_exactly and tests/test_sandbox_projection.py::test_the_stdlib_shape_check_refuses_every_drift keep the producer and the schema in step.

Closed delegate-budget shape check. One test covers both directions: a request of max_model_calls and wall_clock_s is returned as asked; an unknown key, a negative count, a non-integer max_model_calls and a non-object are refused.

Delegation-tree chain and parent/child binding walk (plan 4.6). Sensitivity: a tampered child head is detected (and forged parents/grants, orphans, missing delegate-end by sibling tests). Negative control: an honest parent/child pair verifies.
Host-side op nesting/NUL/non-finite check in strict_loads. One test covers both directions: a carry nested 30 deep decodes to a ToolOp; nested 40 deep is refused with code json.
Prices file vs team lock (C3). One test covers both directions: the rendered prices file loads through the lock; an edited prices file is refused as '(prices changed)' and a symlinked one is refused.
Exact-shape check of a loaded runtime.json. One test covers both directions: the rendered runtime_record is accepted unchanged; the same record with a hand-written api_key is refused.

Team lock re-hash. Sensitivity: an edit to any locked file (agent, TEAM.md, grants, runtime, README) is refused naming that path as '(changed)'. Negative control: an untouched render loads and its lock lists every agent.

Closed run_code input check before the host runs model-supplied code. Had no direct test before this ledger row. Sensitivity: missing/extra keys, an unknown language and non-string fields are refused. Negative control: {language, source, stdin?} is accepted and stdin encoded.
Effective-toolset name check. Had no direct test before this ledger row. Sensitivity: an unknown tool name (shell) is refused. Negative control: every known tool, and the empty toolset, are accepted.
Reserved-key MAC check on model-reply records. One test covers both directions: an entry with the correct MAC is appended; a forged MAC raises 'MAC' and a wrong-shaped entry raises 'shape'.

Transcript hash-chain walk. Sensitivity: an edited, deleted or reordered record makes the chain not verify. Negative control: an untouched three-record transcript verifies, complete, with the journal's head.

Read-path symlink refusal for the brief's WASM grants. One test covers both directions: a symlink out of the project and an in-project alias are refused 'resolves through a symlink'; the real path 'data' is accepted.
Guest argv bound (count, NUL, total bytes). One test covers both directions: flag-like guest args are passed through after '--'; a NUL, 257 args and an oversized arg are refused.

Mount-host spelling check (wasmtime splits --dir on ':'). Sensitivity: any ':' in the host is refused. Negative control: an absolute plain host (/p/data) builds a Mount that the exact-dirs grant check then accepts.
stdin/output-cap bounds. Sensitivity: oversized or str stdin and a zero cap are refused. Negative control: bytes stdin with positive caps executes and returns the output.

Project/runtime mount host containment. Sensitivity: a symlink, .git, a file, a host outside the project, the root itself and a missing dir are refused. Negative control: a real data mount beside a private scratch materializes (the test's second half refuses an overlap).

The pinned wasmtime argv shape (C-3 compute-only boundary). Sensitivity: any extra flag (--dir /, --env, -S inherit-network=y, ...) is refused in grant and parity mode. Negative control: parity mode accepts the ms timeout and component profile spellings.
Guest language allowlist (no native fallback). Sensitivity: ruby, '', Python, None, native and shell are refused before provisioning is asked. Negative control: python builds its argv.

Core-module path check. Sensitivity: a module outside the project, under .agentteams/.git/.claude, a directory and a missing file are refused. Negative control: mods/m.wasm, relative or absolute, is accepted.

A sha256 over the canonical grant JSON that wasm_mcp writes into the launch flags as --grant-sha256. It computes a value and compares nothing; the server refuses a mismatch at start (tests/test_wasm_mcp_server.py::test_refuses_to_start_on_grant_digest_mismatch), and tests/test_wasm_mcp.py::test_grant_digest_matches_the_servers pins parity and that two grants differ.

The tree digest P03 pins, refusing non-regular entries. Sensitivity: an added file changes the digest (resolve_tree refuses 'tree') and a planted symlink is refused 'not a regular file'. Negative control: a plain tree digests to exactly the documented line format.
Render-time text vs per-agent wiring check. One test covers both directions: run_wasm stated but not wired, and wired without its section, are refused; matching claims and wiring pass.
Install-target guard. Sensitivity: installing into / or the home directory is refused. Negative control: a project directory installs every component.
Component-name allowlist. Sensitivity: resolving 'ruby' is refused as an unknown WASM component. Negative control: a pinned component (wasmtime) resolves to its verified entry.

Download-host allowlist (https on DOWNLOAD_HOSTS only). Sensitivity: http and an off-allowlist https host are refused before anything is written. Negative control: a redirect to https://release-assets.githubusercontent.com is accepted (same test refuses off-list redirects).

Generated data: one entry per historical version of the sandbox launcher template, built from git history by scripts/build_launcher_lineage.py. agentteams.launcher_lineage reads it to label a derived launcher current/older/modified; the file itself decides nothing. Byte-for-byte regeneration is pinned by tests/test_launcher_lineage.py::test_lineage_regenerates_byte_for_byte.

Compromise-indicator DATA (file/name/env/grep rules for the litellm 1.107.0 incident). remote.sh embeds it in a quoted heredoc and L1-audit.sh parses and matches it; nothing in it executes or decides. The matcher is L1-audit.sh, registered as a verifier with tests/test_vulnscan_server_kit.py::test_g27_ioc_check_on_a_minimal_host.

Generated corpus of sections earlier templates emitted unfenced, built from git history by scripts/build_template_lineage.py; the merge code consults it as data when deciding whether hand-unfenced text is a known template section. It decides nothing itself; tests/test_template_lineage.py::test_corpus_regenerates_byte_for_byte pins it to its generator.

npm lockfile pinning the Copilot CLI and its platform packages with sha512 integrity values: data that npm ci checks inside the agent Dockerfile, not a check itself. Its pins are asserted by tests/test_vulnscan_copilot_driver.py::test_the_image_builds_copilot_from_the_committed_lockfile.

npm manifest naming the single pinned @github/copilot dependency for the agent image's copilot build stage. It is input data to npm ci; the enforcement (lockfile integrity, tree sha256) is in the Dockerfile stage and npm, not in this file.

A three-line hand-off wrapper: reads one line from stdin into its own environment and execs the given command with stdin closed. It has no condition and no refuse/allow branch; the decision of where the value may go is made by git-credential-vulnscan (registered as a verifier) and by subproc_confine.py, which builds the container argv.

Configuration example: a settings.json hooks block an operator merges by hand to wire constitutional-gate.py as a PreToolUse hook. It decides nothing; the refuse/ask decisions live in the hook script and agentteams.scan. Its wiring is checked by tests such as tests/test_constitutional_gate_hook.py.
